transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess I came in because… nothing really feels like mine anymore. Like, I used to get excited about painting murals, going for runs, playing basketball, even making a really good drink at the bar—there’s a whole rhythm to that, you know? People don’t think about it, but a good pour, the glass, the little twist of lime… anyway.

Now I just kind of stand there and feel like I don’t care about any of it. It’s like I’m watching somebody else’s life, and I don’t know where I went.
Have you lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, like painting murals, running, or playing basketball?

Yeah… yeah, I have. That’s kind of the whole reason I came in, I guess. Those things used to feel like they belonged to me—murals, running, basketball, even making a drink just right at work. Now I’ll be standing there and it’s like… I don’t care. Like I’m just going through the motions.

Funny, because I used to spend forever getting a color right on a wall, like this one blue I mixed once—anyway, it’s not like that now. It all just feels flat.
Have you felt down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for the last couple of weeks?

I don’t know if I’d say it that neatly… “most of the day, nearly every day” sounds like something you’d write on a form. I mean, I’ve been feeling pretty low, yeah, but I don’t really keep track of the hours.

Some days I’m just behind the bar wiping the same spot over and over, and I’ll realize I haven’t really said much to anybody. Then some customer starts talking about the game, and I used to have opinions about that—like real opinions—but now I just kind of nod. So… I don’t know. I’ve felt down a lot, I guess. I just don’t know how to measure it.
Have you felt tired or had little energy most days lately?

Yeah… tired, yeah. It’s weird, because it’s not even like I did some huge thing. Like at work, by the time I carry a couple cases of liquor or set up the well, my body feels like I already worked a double, even if I barely did anything that day.

And I used to move fast back there, you know? There’s a whole setup with the bottles and the ice and making sure the citrus is cut right—anyway, now I’ll do a couple basic things and I’m just… worn out. Like my legs are heavy before the night even starts.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good at things you used to be good at, or like you’re letting people down?

Yeah… I do. I keep thinking I messed things up for people who were counting on me. Like the younger bartenders at work—there’s a couple of them I was supposed to help bring along, show them how to handle a rush, how to talk to people without getting swallowed by it, you know?

And then there were some artists I told I’d help find wall space for, because I used to know people who had spots open… cafés, back rooms, places like that. I keep thinking I wrecked their chance somehow. Like I had a door cracked open for them and then I just… dropped it.

It’s not even just “I feel bad.” It’s more like… I deserve whatever comes down on me for letting them down. Like that’s fair, after what I did to their shot.
Have you been feeling like you’re not good at things you used to be good at, or like you’re letting people down?

Yeah… I mean, I know I already kind of said it, but it’s like it keeps circling back.

I keep thinking about the younger guys at the bar—kids, I call them kids even though they’re grown men—and how I was supposed to show them the ropes. And the artists too, the ones I told I’d help get some wall space for their stuff. I used to know people for that, back when I was still… you know, moving around, talking to everyone.

There was this one coffee shop that had terrible espresso but great light on the back wall—anyway, that’s not the point. The point is I feel like I dropped it. Like I wrecked their shot somehow. And it doesn’t just feel like I made a mistake. It feels like I deserve whatever happens to me because of it.
Have you been feeling like you’re not as good as you used to be, or like you’ve become a burden to others?

Yeah… burden, not exactly like I’m making people carry me around or something, but… I do feel like I’m not who I was for them.

I keep coming back to those younger bartenders I was supposed to help, show them the little stuff—how to keep calm when the bar’s three deep, how to not let some loud guy throw you off. And then the artists too, the ones I told I’d help get wall space. I used to know places, people with back rooms, cafés… one place had this crooked little hallway where paintings actually looked good, even though the owner was a pain.

Anyway… yeah. I feel like I let them down. Like I wrecked their shot somehow. And then I think, whatever happens to me because of that, I probably deserve it.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost pleasure in the things you used to enjoy, like painting, basketball, or making drinks, most days—even when you’re doing them?

Yeah… most days, I think. It’s like nothing feels like mine anymore.

I used to get a charge out of things, you know? Murals especially—seeing a blank wall and thinking about what could go there, even just colors in my head. And going for a run, or playing basketball, or making a drink just right… like when the balance is good and you know it before they even taste it.

Now I’ll be standing there doing it and it’s just… flat. Like I’m watching my hands do something I used to care about, but I don’t feel attached to it. I don’t even know when that started exactly. I came in because that scared me, I guess—because I’m there, but I’m not really in it.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or doing things at a much slower pace than usual?

I don’t know… slower how, exactly?

I mean, I’m not exactly racing around these days, but I haven’t been clocking myself or anything. Behind the bar you kind of move how the night makes you move—if it’s busy, you move, if it’s dead, you end up wiping the same spot on the counter too long. There was this old rag we used to have that never really dried right, smelled like lemons and mildew—sorry, that’s not what you asked.

I guess I haven’t noticed some big change like people saying, “Hey, why are you moving so slow?” Not really. Maybe I feel slowed down inside sometimes, but as far as walking or doing things at a much slower pace… I’m not sure.
Have you noticed that your thoughts have been moving more slowly than usual, or that it takes you longer to process things or make decisions?

Yeah… I think so. Not like I’m stupid all of a sudden, but things that used to just happen don’t happen.

Like inventory at the bar used to be automatic for me. I’d look at the bottles, count them off in my head, know what was low, what needed ordering. Now I’ll stand there staring at the same row of bottles and lose count three times. And then I get irritated because it’s just bottles, you know? It’s not… it’s not supposed to be hard.

Even something dumb like deciding what garnish to restock first—I’ll freeze on it. Limes or cherries or whatever, and I’m just standing there like it’s some big decision. The other night I kept opening the fridge, then closing it, and I remembered this old manager I had who used to label everything with blue tape, wrote like a doctor, completely unreadable… sorry.

But yeah. It takes me longer. My head doesn’t catch the way it used to.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in all activities, to the point where nothing gives you any pleasure anymore, even things you used to really enjoy?

Yeah… that’s why I came in, really. It’s not even just “I’m bored” or whatever. It’s like nothing feels like mine anymore.

I used to get excited about things—murals, especially. I’d see a wall and start thinking colors, shapes, where the light hits it. Or I’d go for a run, play basketball, make a drink just right at work… there’s a kind of satisfaction in that, when the pour is right and the glass looks clean. I used to care about that stuff.

Now I’m just… standing there. Doing it, or thinking about doing it, and there’s nothing. Like I don’t care about any of it, even though I know I used to. I keep waiting for something to catch, and it doesn’t.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost pleasure in *all* activities, to the point where *nothing* gives you any enjoyment anymore, even things you used to really love?

Yeah… I mean, I think that’s what I’m trying to say. It’s not that I can’t name things I used to like—I can. Murals, running, basketball, making a drink the right way. I used to feel something from those.

Now it’s like I’m there but not really in it. I’ll look at a wall and know, in my head, I used to think about colors and lines and all that, but there’s no pull. Same with a good drink at work—clean glass, right pour, all of it—and it just feels like… tasks.

So, yeah. Nothing really gives me enjoyment right now. That’s kind of why I came in. Nothing feels like mine anymore.

Would you say that absolutely nothing gives you pleasure anymore—not just the big things like painting or playing basketball, but even small, everyday moments, like a good conversation, a cup of coffee, or something as simple as sunlight coming through a window?

Yeah… I mean, that’s kind of it. I came in because nothing feels like mine anymore.

I used to get excited about stuff—murals, going for a run, playing basketball, even making a drink right at work. Like, there was a little pride in it, you know? The glass, the pour, the way it looked on the bar. Now I just kind of stand there like… okay, I’m doing this, but I don’t care.

Even when I try to notice something small, it doesn’t really land. It’s like I remember that I’m supposed to enjoy things, but I don’t actually feel it.
